name: list_chat_artifacts
description: List all published artifact versions in a conversation, with metadata, versions, groups and URLs. Paginated; files remain private unless explicitly shared.

name: read_chat_artifact
description: Download the original bytes of a conversation artifact as bounded base64 chunks, including private files. Start at offset 0, decode each data chunk and append bytes until nextOffset is null. file.digest is the SHA-256 of the complete file.

name: set_chat_artifact_visibility
description: Enable or revoke a public link for one artifact version in any conversation. Only make files public when the user requests sharing. Returns visibility and publicUrl; revocation cannot remove downloaded copies.

name: list_chat_attachments
description: List files attached to a conversation, including files not yet sent. Paginated.

name: read_chat_attachment
description: Download an attachment as bounded base64 chunks. Start at offset 0, decode each data chunk and append bytes until nextOffset is null. file.digest is the SHA-256 of the complete file.

name: get_chat_backend_migration
description: Preview an explicit backend change without changing anything. Select chatId or runId. Reports authorized destinations, failure details and, while the working environment exists, the warning that the change discards its working files (history, attachments and artifacts are kept). pending is true while the change waits for the previous execution to stop. An expired environment has no working files to lose.

name: migrate_chat_backend
description: Explicitly change a conversation or mission backend on an authorized node. Select chatId or runId and confirm. VM and native execution never share a node: with an existing working environment this is a node change, which also requires discardWorkingFiles: true. The environment expires: its working files, unpushed changes and installed tools are lost; the conversation history, attachments and artifacts are kept. The running turn stops; a chat waits for its next message (queued messages and scheduled waits start on the destination) and an active mission resumes there automatically. The first new environment waits for capacity on the destination while it stays authorized. Native provenance, administrator approvals and live management grants remain enforced. An expired environment selects its new backend without discardWorkingFiles; the next message creates an empty environment.
